Choose by how you review changes

Start with Cursor if you want to work inside its code editor and inspect changes there. Try Claude Code if a terminal-driven repair task fits your existing workflow. Both products offer CLI automation, so the useful comparison is how you review a patch, constrain tools and verify the result on your own account.

Current CLI instructions support non-interactive print mode in both tools. Available commands, models and approval behavior depend on the installed version and configuration. Review the current official instructions before scripting a run; a terminal interface does not itself isolate files or network access.

Download the same small repository task

The starter contains a deliberately faulty order-summary function, a written contract and twelve fixed tests. It needs Node.js 22 or later, no package installation and no network request to run the checks. Review code produced by an assistant before executing it.

Download the repair-task ZIPDownload the exact trial prompt
cd coding-trial
node --test --test-reporter=tap test/orders.test.mjs

The starter passes 2 of 12 checks. A failure at this stage is expected. The checks cover paid-order filtering, exact integer cents, refunds, lexical ID order and tie-breaking, input mutation, duplicate IDs, invalid decimals and integer overflow. They are public exercise cases, not hidden evaluation data.

  1. Unpack two separate copies. Keep the starter and test file unchanged as a baseline.
  2. Give each product the same prompt. It requests edits only in src/orders.mjs, with no dependencies, network, shell execution or other agents.
  3. Save the first patch and reply before correcting anything. Review the diff, then independently run the twelve checks.
  4. Verify the test file against the original ZIP. Record setup failures, refused operations and correction prompts, including runs that never complete.

The configured CLI run is not an Anthropic Claude-model benchmark. We retained the tool identity and returned model label separately; the underlying provider identity was not independently verified. This is not a matched-model comparison, and it does not establish a winner over Cursor.

The run could read and edit fixture files. Shell tools, Chrome integration and MCP servers were disabled for it; we ran the checks separately after reviewing the patch. The account plan and actual billed usage were not established. No execution-speed or cost winner is claimed.

Retained first reply · Retained first patch · Independent test output · Run conditions

The all-green test report still missed two contract violations. After reading the patch, we separately tried a numeric amount (amount: 1) and a null refund (refund: null). The configured CLI patch accepted both; the written contract requires decimal strings and defaults only a missing refund. Our author-written reference rejected both. These two checks were chosen after the run, so they are review findings, not a preregistered head-to-head score. Inspect both exact inputs and observations.

The twelve public tests remain unchanged. Keep the green report alongside the diff review and the extra boundary findings. Test files that were changed, disabled or substituted cannot be treated as a valid comparison.

Mark a run incomplete if setup, permissions or usage limits stopped it. Compare the actual patch and the amount of review work, then repeat on tasks representative of your repository. Keep any first failure rather than replacing it with the corrected result.

Interpret a trial without overclaiming

A model inside a coding product, its tool permissions and its surrounding application can all affect the outcome. Record them separately. CLI and editor trials are also different experiences; this fixture does not measure autocomplete, large-repository navigation, multi-file reliability, accessibility or team administration.

When test results are tied, inspect untested edge cases and the clarity of the diff. Count human corrections and setup effort. Verify current plan limits on the account you will use; do not multiply one CLI-reported estimate into a monthly cost forecast.
